claim: There exists one compactly supported absolutely continuous probability measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb R\) such that, for every \(0<\beta<1/3\), \[|\widehat{\mu}(\xi)|\le C_\beta(1+|\xi|)^{-\beta}\quad(\xi\in\mathbb R),\] while the dyadic lacunary maximal operator \(M_\mu f(x)=\sup_{k\in\mathbb Z}|f*\mu_k(x)|\) is unbounded from \(H^1(\mathbb R)\) to \(L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R)\).

correctness.rationale: The concentration argument proves the uniform point-set estimate; exact integration gives the sinc factor; the three frequency ranges prove decay for each \(\beta<1/3\). The modified spike width still fits the atom on a linear number of dyadic scales, and the superlacunary mixture's lower- and higher-index terms are controlled by the stated density and L1 bounds. The resulting weak-\(L^1\) lower bound diverges as \(q^{m+1}\).
